summary: Full backend + frontend testing of Portech. Backend: 11/11 pytest tests passed (root, contact POST valid/invalid/missing fields/project_type, contact GET without _id, status regression). Frontend: all key flows working — Home hero, 4 nav links, Services page (4 blocks), About page (Mission, Vision, chapters 01-05), Contact form success ('Demande envoyée'), invalid email blocked, mobile nav toggle, CTA -> /contact, no broken images, no console errors.
action_items: Note: review_request listed the À-propos desktop nav testid as 'nav-link-a-propos', but the Navbar regex /\s|à|é/g strips the 'à' character, producing actual testid 'nav-link-propos' (desktop) and 'mobile-nav-link-propos' (mobile). Functionally fine, but consider normalising testid suffixes (e.g. using a stable slug like 'apropos' or 'about') to make selectors more predictable.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is compact and clean; ContactSubmissionCreate uses EmailStr + constrained lengths correctly; returns 201 with UUID + ISO datetime.
GET /api/contact projects out _id via find({}, {'_id': 0}) — good.
No authentication on GET /api/contact — any visitor can list submissions. Consider an admin auth guard before production.
CORS allow_origins defaults to '*' with allow_credentials=True which browsers reject together; tighten CORS_ORIGINS in env for prod.
Navbar testid slug derivation from label via regex is brittle (removes 'à','é') and couples testids to French copy; prefer explicit slugs per link.
seed_data_creation: Created a few TEST_-prefixed contact submissions and one TEST_client status record via API tests and Playwright success flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend URL env var: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_portech_api.py covers root, contact POST/GET, status regression. For frontend, desktop nav testid for À propos is 'nav-link-propos' (not 'nav-link-a-propos'); mobile uses 'mobile-nav-link-*' prefix. Contact form success component has data-testid='contact-success' and text contains 'Demande envoyée'. Invalid email is blocked by HTML5 email type validity; contact-error shows after submit attempt. Hero h1 uses CSS text-transform:uppercase, so innerText is uppercase — use case-insensitive comparison.
rca of the issue: No production bugs found. Only naming convention remark on auto-generated testids from French labels.
